title: Grateful Dead Live at P.N.E. Coliseum on 1973-06-22
lineage: composite: MSR> PCM> DAT> CD> EAC> WAV> SHN; MAC> R> R> CD> DAT> WAV> SHN; MSR> C> DAT> CD> EAC> WAV> SHN

ai_review.summary: Matrix‑derived recording with crystal‑clear soundboard later in the set, showcasing a legendary Bird Song, monster Playin' in the Band and an epic Other One.
ai_review.review: The show is consistently praised as one of the top ’73 performances – loose yet inspired playing, a soaring Bird Song, scorching Sunshine Daydream, massive Playin' in the Band, and a marathon Other One that many call sublime.  The source is a soundboard‑plus‑audience matrix; early discs suffer volume dips and splice artifacts, but the later portions are crystal clear with excellent separation of instruments.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 30 reviews, almost all 4–5 stars, uniformly praising both musical performance and sound quality despite minor splice/volume issues; the weighted average yields a high rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Early discs have volume variations and AUD splices (notably in The Other One), but later tracks are crystal‑clear with beautiful instrument separation; audience patches fill holes, overall a very listenable matrix mix.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Loose and relaxed first half that builds into a high‑energy second set; Bird Song kicks the momentum, followed by seamless jams and extended improvisations leading to an epic Other One and closing with a blazing Sugar Magnolia.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Described as humble, gentle, creative; notable guitar riffs around the 10‑minute mark and inventive ideas throughout the jams.
band_member_comments.Phil: Repeatedly highlighted for his creative solo work (one of the longest ever), melodic harmonies on Black Peter, and overall “force” in the band’s interplay.
band_member_comments.Bob: Praised for taking lead on China Cat, delivering a strong lead‑guitar lick that showcases his ability to carry the tune.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith's organ/keyboard is noted as prominent and beautiful, especially during verses of Sunshine Daydream and other sections.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill (and Mickey in later years) receive thanks for keeping the band tight; no specific critiques beyond general praise.
